deep.reconstruction:
Setting. (C, W, Cof) is a category with weak equivalences and cofibrations satisfying Baues' axioms C1–C3 for a 'cofibration category'. These are H.-J. Baues, Obstruction Theory, LNM 628 (1977), later Algebraic Homotopy (1989):
- C1: composition and 2-out-of-3.
- C2: pushouts along cofibrations exist, and cofibrations and trivial cofibrations are stable under them.
- C3: every map factors as a cofibration followed by a weak equivalence.
Grothendieck adds the assumption that there is an initial object ∅. Cof then denotes the full subcategory of cofibrant objects (∅ → x a cofibration), and W_cof is the weak equivalences between them.

Claim (stated as 'known'). The inclusion Cof → C induces an equivalence W_cof^{-1}Cof → W^{-1}C. To prove it, he builds a quasi-inverse L: W^{-1}C → W_cof^{-1}Cof, i.e. a functor C → W_cof^{-1}Cof inverting W.

Step 1, cofibrant replacement. Apply C3 to ∅ → x to get x̃ → x with x̃ cofibrant and α_x: x̃ → x in W.

Step 2, lifting a map f: x → y. Consider the square ∅ → ỹ, ∅ → x̃, fα_x: x̃ → y, α_y: ỹ → y (in W). The 'weak lifting lemma' (Baues' lifting lemma) gives:
- a trivial cofibration i: ỹ → ỹ';
- a map α'_y: ỹ' → y with α'_y i = α_y (so α'_y ∈ W by 2-of-3);
- a map φ̃: x̃ → ỹ' with α'_y φ̃ = fα_x.
So φ̃ lifts fα_x not to ỹ but to an enlargement ỹ'. Define L(f) = [i]^{-1}[φ̃] in Hom_{W_cof^{-1}Cof}(x̃, ỹ).

Step 3, independence of choices. Given two choices (i_1, α'_1, φ_1) and (i_2, α'_2, φ_2), form the pushout ỹ'_3 = ỹ'_1 ∨_ỹ ỹ'_2. By C2, ỹ → ỹ'_3 is again a trivial cofibration, and α'_1, α'_2 glue to a map ỹ'_3 → y. One may therefore assume ('OPS' = on peut supposer) a common ỹ', i, α'. Everything then reduces to a lemma.

Lemma: if x', y' are cofibrant, α: y' → y is in W, and αφ = αψ for φ, ψ: x' ⇉ y', then [φ] = [ψ] in W_cof^{-1}Cof.

The bottom-left diagrams sketch the intended proof. The map (φ,ψ): x'⊔x' → y' and the codiagonal ∇: x'⊔x' → x' agree after composing to y. This is the setup for factoring ∇ through a cylinder and applying the weak lifting lemma again to obtain a homotopy, after a further trivial cofibration y' → y''. The next page indeed shows cylinder diagrams (x∨x → C → y).

Step 4. Given the lemma, he asserts that u ↦ L(u) is compatible with identities and compositions 'immédiatement', so one gets the functor C → W_cof^{-1}Cof.

Purpose. This is the opening page of the 'Champs 3' manuscript. Grothendieck is reworking the basic homotopy-category comparison in Baues' cofibration-category framework, presumably as groundwork for the homotopy-theoretic side of the stacks / Pursuing Stacks programme (c. 1982–83).
errors: The lemma ([φ]=[ψ] when αφ=αψ with α ∈ W) is stated but not proved on this page. The intended proof (factor ∇: x'⊔x' → Cyl x' → x' by C3, apply the weak lifting lemma to get a homotopy H: Cyl x' → y'' with y' → y'' a trivial cofibration, then use [i_0] = [i_1], since both are sections of the weak equivalence Cyl x' → x') is only sketched in diagrams. It is correct, but needs x'⊔x' to be cofibrant; this holds by C2 since x' is cofibrant.

Compatibility with composition is called 'immédiate'. It actually requires lifting a composite and comparing via the independence lemma: one must push the lift for g out along the enlargement used for f. Easy, but not literally immediate.

Independence from the choice of the replacement α_x itself is not addressed. It is not needed if the choice is fixed once per object, but the natural isomorphisms L∘incl ≅ id and incl∘L ≅ id, required for the equivalence, are not yet written.
Minor: in the pushout reduction one must also check that [i_3]^{-1}[k_1φ_1] = [i_1]^{-1}[φ_1]. This follows from k_1 i_1 = i_3 and k_1 ∈ W, which is left implicit.

ideas.what: Equivalence W_cof^{-1}Cof ≃ W^{-1}C for a cofibration category (Baues axioms C1–C3 plus initial object), proved via cofibrant replacement and a quasi-inverse functor
ideas.modern_name: Homotopy category of a cofibration category (Waldhausen/Brown/Baues category) is equivalent to that of its cofibrant objects; cofibrant replacement functor
ideas.usually_credited_to: K. S. Brown (1973, dual fibration-category version); H.-J. Baues (Obstruction Theory 1977, Algebraic Homotopy 1989); Quillen (1967) for model categories
ideas.where_published: Pursuing Stacks (1983) discusses model categories and 'modelizers' but I am unsure whether Baues' axioms or this lemma appear there

ideas.what: 'Weak lifting lemma': a map from a cofibrant object to y lifts through a weak equivalence ỹ → y after enlarging ỹ by a trivial cofibration
ideas.modern_name: Lifting lemma in cofibration categories (Baues II.1.11-type lemma); approximate lifting without fibrations

ideas.what: Maps φ, ψ out of a cofibrant object that are equalized by a weak equivalence become equal in the localization (via a cylinder on x'⊔x' → x')
ideas.modern_name: Left homotopy via cylinder objects; equality in Ho of maps coequalized by a weak equivalence

ideas.what: Reduction of independence-of-choice via the pushout ỹ'_1 ∨_ỹ ỹ'_2 of two trivial cofibrations
ideas.modern_name: Standard amalgamation/pushout argument in cofibration categories

missed.claim: Historical: this documents Grothendieck working directly with Baues' cofibration-category axioms (C1–C3) around 1982. That is an engagement with Baues' Obstruction Theory not usually mentioned in accounts of the background to Pursuing Stacks.
missed.quote: Soit (C, W_e, cof) une catégorie satisfaisant C1 à C3 de Baues
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is minor provenance information for historians tracing which abstract-homotopy frameworks (Quillen, Brown, Baues) Grothendieck read before Pursuing Stacks and Les Dérivateurs. The mathematics itself is standard.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a careful but standard proof that cofibrant objects compute the homotopy category of a Baues cofibration category. All of it is well known (Brown 1973, Baues 1977/1989). The only mildly interesting point is the explicit reference to Baues' axioms in Grothendieck's 1982 notes.
transcription_corrections: The added line reads approximately 'Ou supposons qu'il y a objet initial ∅' (insertion above the first line).
The parenthetical '(P. ex on pourrait avoir cof = W cof_{we})' is uncertain. It may read 'cof = cof_{we}' or refer to cofibrations being weak equivalences; the image is ambiguous.
In the reduction step the text reads roughly '(écrivant g = fα_x, y' au lieu de ỹ', x' au lieu de x̃, mais x' cof)', i.e. x' is cofibrant.
The lifted map is written φ̃ (tilde over φ); the choice triple is (i, α'_y, φ).
